summary: This work demonstrates parametrically driven multi-qubit couplers based on dc-SQUIDs and tunable SNAILs for realizing high-fidelity gates between any pair of qubits in a four-qubit plaquette, including diagonal couplings, as well as native three- and four-qubit interactions. By carefully analyzing the Jacobi-Anger expansion of the time-dependent Hamiltonian and optimizing the drive parameters, the authors achieve $\sqrt{\mathrm{iSWAP}}$ gates with 99.9% fidelity in 50 ns for two qubits and 95% fidelity in 200 ns for three-qubit gates, while also demonstrating simultaneous execution of two disjoint two-qubit gates at 99.4% fidelity.
motivation: Multi-qubit couplers can enhance connectivity in superconducting quantum processors and enable direct gates between non-nearest-neighbor qubits without requiring SWAP-based routing, reducing circuit depth and coupler overhead by approximately a factor of two in 2D arrays.
method: The authors modeled dc-SQUID and SNAIL couplers capacitively coupled to four transmon qubits (with detunings spanning 5.5–7.1 GHz for the SQUID setup), applied the irrotational gauge to correctly handle time-dependent external flux drives, and expanded the driven Hamiltonian using Jacobi-Anger expansions to identify resonance conditions for selective interactions. Full four-qubit Hilbert space simulations with QuTiP using super-Gaussian pulse envelopes (rank $r=8$) optimized gate fidelities via parameter tuning and Z-phase corrections.
result: iSWAP gates achieved 99.9% (4-qubit) and 99.98% (2-qubit subsystem) fidelity in 48–64 ns across all geometries; parallel two-qubit gates reached 99.35% fidelity; three-qubit native gates ($a_1^\dagger a_2^\dagger a_3 + \mathrm{h.c.}$) achieved 95.5% fidelity in 200 ns and require only 54 CNOT equivalents versus 93 gates for standard decomposition; four-qubit gates gave 79.3% fidelity in 46 ns but remain limited by weak coupling strength.
